sentence: This project studies how hyperglycemia and Hedgehog signaling affect T cells in type 2 diabetes-associated breast cancer.
This project supports research that uses omics technology and computational biology to study the onset and progression of disease.
This project tries to find out whether long-term metabolic measurements can predict complications of diabetes, such as nerve and kidney damage.
This project tests aspirin as a contrast agent for magnetic resonance imaging of inflammation and maps aspirin metabolites in thin tissue sections.
This project studies how impaired inhibition in the striatum relates to autism in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome.
This project studies how temperature affects the function of an ion channel called calcium homeostasis modulator 2.
This project tests whether rheologic disturbances in the microvasculature contribute to organ failure in sepsis and whether blood transfusion can change them.
This project develops a diagnostic platform that detects mutations in cell-free DNA from blood samples to diagnose lung cancer early.
This project sets up a mass spectrometer to study proteins and other molecules in rare samples, such as individual cells from the brain or blood.
This project follows autistic and non-autistic youth from childhood into adolescence to study social communication, social motivation and friendships.
This project maps histopathology in the inner ear and builds a computational model to improve speech perception for cochlear implant listeners.
This project studies how social factors shape sexual risk and HIV testing among Latino/x sexual minority migrant men.
This project provides genomic services, such as sequencing and gene expression profiling, for studying genes in cancer cells and tumors.
This project oversees and coordinates the program projects and cores, including their fiscal oversight and progress evaluation.
This project uses specially bred mice to study how certain genes affect immune cells that attack their own body, focusing on the mitochondria.
This project creates genetically engineered mice, including gene knockout and gene knockin mice, for studying food allergy.
This project studies the regulatory mechanisms of human spermatogonial stem cells and their surrounding microenvironment in the testis.
This project studies how the metabolic state of glioblastoma determines how tumors generate proteins that promote their growth and resistance to radiation and chemotherapy.
This project studies how psychosocial and cultural factors relate to cardiometabolic health among older Chinese Americans.
This project studies how skin melanoma resists therapy and tries to develop combination therapies that target these resistance mechanisms.
